atoms.text: My name is Coto. Which is pretty weird I think. At least I don’t know any other Cotos. Do you? Who wants to have a name with a toe on the end? My mum says I should be proud to have such a strong name. I was named after the most famous Ecuadorian volcano, Cotopaxi, which is still active. My mum is from Ecuador, and she’s a geologist. I guess it made sense to her. She said she wanted me to be active and powerful and blah blah blah. Maybe I’ll grow into it. At least I am not confused with other Cotos. That’s a plus.

atoms.sound: What is one thing Kohtoh doesn’t like about his name?
b: His name is hard to spell.

atoms.a: What is one thing Coto likes about his name?
atoms.sound: What is one thing Kohtoh likes about his name?
b: ++He is never confused with other kids of the same name.
He likes being named after an active volcano.

atoms.text: I usually wish my mum was more normal. Sometimes when she picks me up from school, she’s so excited about a new rock or geode or something that she shows it to me in front of everybody else. They all look at her weirdly. And by her, I mean me. My dad is also a geologist. As a family, we talk about rocks a lot. Sometimes, I accidentally reveal how much I know about rocks at school in front of the other kids. I always end up wishing I had just said nothing.

Sometimes I accidentally reveal how much I know about rocks at school in front of the other kids. <break time='300ms'/>I always end up wishing I had just said nothing.</voice>

atoms.text: I guess there are also advantages to having geologists as parents. We take amazing holidays to all sorts of cool places. My parents don’t call them holidays, they’re “work-trips”. They act like they are holidays though. They are always excited, even more than I am. One year, I got to visit my mum’s family in Ecuador and see the volcano I was named after. I guess that is where it all began. What happened next helped me realise what I wanted to be: a detective!
